On Bayesian logistic regression posteriors for two standard data sets, which satisfy these assumptions, the gradient cost of the chain with the non-reversibly updated uniform grows roughly like the square root of the condition number at the posterior mode, and that of standard adjusted OBABO roughly like its $3/4$ power.
item.dc:creator: Nawaf Bou-Rabee

item.title: Operator limits of random matrices: Edge universality and sharp approximations
item.description: arXiv:2610.35808v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish operator universality at the spectral edge of general Wigner matrices by showing that their suitably rescaled Lanczos tridiagonalizations, constructed from deterministic initial vectors, converge to the stochastic Airy operator with Dirichlet boundary condition. The result requires control of the entire tridiagonal structure on the scale relevant to the limiting differential operator. The Lanczos coefficients for non-Gaussian Wigner matrices are strongly dependent. We analyze their fluctuations by combining multi-resolvent local laws with quantitative control of Krylov subspaces and a comparison of the resulting Jacobi coefficients with those of the Gaussian ensembles. This approach identifies the limiting Brownian potential directly from the original matrix entries, without invoking Dyson Brownian motion in the step of Green function comparison. The resolvent limit yields joint convergence of edge eigenvalues, embedded eigenfunctions, and spectral measures. For Gaussian, Laguerre and circular $\beta$-ensembles we construct sharp couplings to the stochastic Airy, Bessel and Sine operators, preserving the finite-matrix laws. For fixed $\beta > 0$, their squared Hilbert-Schmidt inverse errors have almost-sure orders $n^{-1/3}, n^{-1}$ and $n^{-1}$, respectively, with $a > 0$ in the hard-edge upper bound. We also identify the positive leading order coefficient for the circular ensemble, whose second derivative jumps at $\beta = 2$.
item.dc:creator: Hyung-Gil Kwak

item.title: The Robust Newton Method for Polynomials and its Polynomiography
item.description: arXiv:2003.00372v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the Robust Newton Method (RNM) for a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $n\geq2$, with continuous map $F(z)=z-p(z)\overline{p'(z)}/(9A(z)^2)$, where $A(z)=\max_{0\leq j\leq n}|p^{(j)}(z)|/j!$. Its fixed points are the roots and critical points; elsewhere it strictly decreases $|p|$ along the Newton direction. The Geometric Modulus Principle inspires the construction and supplies an escape step at nonroot critical points. Every root has an open basin. When nonroot critical points are simple, almost every seed converges to a root, and root-basin boundaries lie in countably many Lipschitz curves with Hausdorff dimension one when nonempty. These conclusions apply after any sufficiently small nonzero linear perturbation $p(z)+\delta z$. Every RNM orbit, with or without escapes, converges to a root or critical point. A hybrid enforcing one RNM update every $T$ iterations retains convergence and reaches $|p(z)p'(z)|\leq\varepsilon$ in $O(T/\varepsilon^2)$ updates, with constants depending on the polynomial and seed; $T=1$ gives RNM. Orbits approaching simple roots eventually reach Smale's $\alpha$-certification, permitting a permanent Newton switch and $O(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))$ further steps for absolute root error $\varepsilon$. For cubics, deterministic critical-point initialization yields an explicit preparatory bound, retained by an RNM-guided Newton refinement. Illustrative computations cover cubics and degree-ten polynomials. For $p(z)=z^n-1$, the basins are exactly the open Voronoi regions, with boundary points converging to the origin. Polynomiographs illustrate basin geometry and iteration-based coloring.
item.dc:creator: Bahman Kalantari

item.title: High-performance computing for the BGK model of the Boltzmann equation with a meshfree Arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian method
item.description: arXiv:2408.02350v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we present high-performance computing for the BGK model of the Boltzmann equation with a mesh-free method. For the numerical simulation of the BGK equation, we use an Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) method developed in previous work, where the approximation of spatial derivatives and the reconstruction of a function are based on the weighted least squares method. A Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) is used to accelerate the code. The result is compared with sequential and parallel versions of the CPU code. Two- and three-dimensional driven cavity problems are solved, where a speed-up of several orders of magnitude is obtained compared to a sequential CPU simulation. The transport step is implemented as a node-parallel CUDA kernel for both two- and three-dimensional physical space: one GPU thread advances one particle-velocity-node pair by tracing its characteristic foot point and reconstructing the distribution there with a register-resident weighted least squares solve. For the three-dimensional case, no velocity reduction is applicable: a single distribution function $f$ is evolved on the full $N_v^3$ velocity grid, so the transport in every coordinate direction follows the resolved velocity node. The device memory footprint is kept at exactly twice the distribution storage by a structure-of-arrays layout with a single transport buffer; particle management runs on the host, so no device-side scratch copies of the cloud are required.
item.dc:creator: Panchatchram Mariappan, Klaas Willems, Gangadhara Boregowda, Sudarshan Tiwari, Axel Klar

item.title: Regularized Unbalanced Optimal Transport with Pearson Marginal Penalties
item.description: arXiv:2503.15105v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study quadratically regularized unbalanced optimal transport with Pearson marginal penalties and a lower bound $\delta\ge0$ on the plan, including the sparse case $\delta=0$. We organize the analysis around the active interface, where the plan switches from its lower bound to larger values. We prove a Newton remainder estimate that depends linearly on the marginal measure of the boundary layer around this interface, and a maximum-norm inverse estimate uniform over all Newton derivatives and cell volumes. Together they give local superlinear convergence of semismooth Newton iteration in function space, of q-order at least $1+\alpha$ when the boundary-layer measure is $O(t^\alpha)$, and a common convergence neighborhood along each refinement sequence whose data converge uniformly. Transverse interfaces give second-order supercloseness of the discrete potentials to the cell averages of the continuum potentials. A directional curvature condition on the input data verifies the interface condition before the solution is known and yields an explicit Newton convergence radius on all sufficiently fine meshes, uniformly in the lower bound. A globalized inexact semismooth Newton iteration has mesh-independent numbers of outer iterations and of full-array operations, that is, passes over the plan array. Its output satisfies an a posteriori error bound relative to the continuum optimal plan. Experiments test the rates at transverse interfaces and at interfaces with tangencies, the curvature criterion, and the algorithmic work. All estimates hold for a fixed regularization parameter and a fixed lower bound on the densities.
item.dc:creator: Minh-Nhat Phung, Minh-Binh Tran

item.title: Asymptotically accurate and geometric locking-free finite element implementation of a refined shell theory
item.description: arXiv:2503.23369v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate finite element analysis of refined shell theories is crucial but often hindered by membrane and shear locking effects. While various element-based locking-free techniques exist, this work addresses the problem at the theoretical level by utilizing results from asymptotic analysis. A formulation of a 2D refined shell theory incorporating transverse shear is developed using rescaled coordinates and angles of rotation, ensuring equal asymptotic orders of magnitude for extension, bending, and rotation measures and their respective stiffnesses. This novel approach, implemented via isogeometric analysis, is shown to be both asymptotically accurate relative to the underlying refined shell theory and inherently free from membrane and shear locking. Numerical simulations of semi-cylindrical shells show excellent agreement between the analytical solutions, 2D refined shell theory predictions, and 3D elasticity theory, validating the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed formulation.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 446 (2025) 118327
item.dc:creator: Khanh Chau Le, Hoang-Giang Bui

item.title: fastGMRES: Robust randomized GMRES via flexible GMRES
item.description: arXiv:2506.18408v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a practical randomized algorithm for solving large sparse systems of linear equations. The algorithm, termed fastGMRES, uses flexible GMRES as an outer wrapper for sketched GMRES together with a practical residual bound to terminate the inner iteration. We demonstrate that fastGMRES requires very little parameter tuning, while still being efficient and robust in the sense of generating non-increasing residual norms. We observe that the inner sketched GMRES method can be run without any inner product computations and vector--vector updates on high-dimensional vectors, yielding significant speedup for many problems.
item.dc:creator: Stefan G\"uttel, John W. Pearson

item.title: A Computational Method for the Inverse Robin Problem with Convergence Rate
item.description: arXiv:2509.17571v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The inverse Robin problem consists in determining the Robin parameter in an elliptic partial differential equation posed on a domain $\Omega$. In this work it is assumed that the right-hand sides of the elliptic problem are known, that the associated solution is available on a subdomain $\omega \subset \Omega$ and that this solution vanishes at most at isolated points on the boundary $\partial \Omega$. Within this framework, a computational method for the reconstruction of the Robin parameter is established, which is inspired by a unique continuation method. The proposed scheme relies solely on first-order Lagrange finite elements ensuring a straightforward implementation. Under the main assumption that the Robin parameter is in a finite dimensional space of continuously differentiable functions it is shown that the numerical method is second order convergent in the finite element's mesh size. For noisy data this convergence rate is shown to hold true until the noise term dominates the error estimate. Numerical experiments are presented that highlight the feasibility of the Robin parameter reconstruction and that confirm the theoretical convergence results numerically.
item.dc:creator: Erik Burman, Marvin Kn\"oller, Lauri Oksanen

item.title: Multiprecision computations with Schwarz methods
item.description: arXiv:2509.20937v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Schwarz methods and preconditioners, where the approximate solution of the local problems is performed at a lower precision, i.e., with fewer digits of accuracy than in the underlying (double precision) computation. Conditions for the appropriate round-off criteria for the lower precision are presented. It is found experimentally that for the model problems about 5 digits of accuracy are sufficient to achieve the theoretical restrictions, and thus, single precision suffices for the local solves. Several numerical experiments illustrate the obtained results.
item.dc:creator: Michal Outrata, Daniel B. Szyld

item.title: An energy- and helicity-conserving enriched galerkin method for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2512.20109v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop an enriched Galerkin (EG) method for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations that conserves both kinetic energy and helicity in the inviscid limit without introducing any additional projection variables. The method employs an EG velocity space, which is the first-order continuous Galerkin space enriched with piecewise constants defined on mesh faces, together with piecewise-constant pressure. Two numerical schemes based on the rotational form of the convective term are proposed: a nonlinear scheme and a linear variant. Both schemes exactly preserve the discrete helicity and kinetic energy, and the Picard iteration maintains the conservation properties of the nonlinear scheme. We prove the conservation properties of both the methods, and establish stability and rigorous error estimates for the nonlinear scheme. Numerical examples demonstrate the accuracy and conservation of the proposed linear scheme.
item.dc:creator: Siyuan Tong, Qilong Zhai, Qian Zhang, Ran Zhang

item.title: Explicit complex time integrators for stiff problems
item.description: arXiv:2601.07730v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Most numerical methods for time integration use real-valued time steps. Complex time steps, however, can provide an additional degree of freedom, as we can select the magnitude of the time step in both the real and imaginary directions. We show that specific paths in the complex time plane lead to expanded stability regions, providing clear computational advantages for complex-valued systems. In particular, we highlight the Schr\"odinger equation, for which complex time integrators can be uniquely optimal. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these benefits extend to certain classes of real-valued stiff systems by coupling complex time steps with the Projective Integration method.
item.dc:creator: Jithin D. George, Julian Koellermeier, Samuel Y. Jung, Niall M. Mangan

item.title: Nonlinear Inverse Iterations for Spin-Orbit Coupled Quantum Gases
item.description: arXiv:2601.08990v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work concerns the computation of ground states of two-component spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates (SO-coupled BECs), modelled by a coupled nonlinear eigenvalue problem of Gross-Pitaevskii type. In regimes with strongly modulated densities, including supersolid-like phases, conventional numerical approaches such as generalized inverse iterations or gradient descent may converge slowly. To address this issue, we apply the J-method [E. Jarlebring, S. Kvaal, W. Michiels. SIAM J. Sci. Comput. 36-4, 2014], which allows nonlinear inverse iterations to be accelerated through spectral shifting. A central analytical challenge arises from global phase invariance, which causes the target eigenvalue of the J-operator to be multiple and prevents the direct application of existing convergence results based on simple eigenvalues. Under a quasi-isolation assumption, we establish that this eigenvalue has algebraic and geometric multiplicity exactly two. By introducing an auxiliary phase-fixed iteration, we prove local linear convergence rates for the shifted J-method, determined by spectral gaps, in a quotient metric modulo global phase rotations. The particle densities converge at the same rate. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted linear convergence for fixed shifts and indicate superlinear convergence for adaptively chosen shifts.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Henning, Laura Huynh

item.title: Stability analysis of Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian ADER-DG methods on classical and degenerate spacetime geometries
item.description: arXiv:2602.09198v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we present a thorough von Neumann stability analysis of explicit and implicit Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) ADER discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods on classical and degenerate spacetime geometries for hyperbolic equations. First, we rigorously study CFL stability conditions for the explicit ADER-DG method, confirming results widely used in the literature while specifying their limitations. Moreover, we discuss stability bounds for ALE methods and characterize the admissible range of grid velocities once a target CFL is fixed. Next, we extend the stability study to ADER-DG in the presence of degenerate spacetime elements, with zero size at the beginning and the end of the time step, but with a non zero spacetime volume. This kind of elements has been introduced in a series of articles on direct ALE methods by Gaburro et al. to connect via spacetime control volumes regenerated Voronoi tessellations after a topology change. Here, we imitate this behavior in a 1d surrogate setting by fictitiously inserting degenerate elements in between two cells. We show that over this simplified degenerate spacetime geometry, both for the explicit and implicit ADER-DG, the von Neumann analysis leads to the same CFL stability conditions as those for classical geometries, laying the theoretical foundations for their use in the context of ALE methods.
item.dc:creator: Mauro Bonafini, Davide Torlo, Elena Gaburro

item.title: Block Diagonalization and Multiplicativity of Quaternion $Z$-Block Circulant Matrices with Applications
item.description: arXiv:2602.11493v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The motivation of this paper is twofold. We firstly investigate the block-diagonalization of the $z$-block circulant matrix $\mathtt{bcirc_z}(\mathcal A)$, and develop the algorithm $\mathtt{bcirc_z}$-inv for computing the inverse of $\mathtt{bcirc_z}(\mathcal A)$. Second, we establish the multiplicativity of the operator $\mathtt{bcirc_z}$, which yields the equivalence between the QT-product of tensors and the multiplication of their corresponding $z$-block circulant matrices. As applications of these results, we conduct large-scale numerical experiments and analyze the scalability of the Tikhonov-regularized model. We also obtain polar decompositions under the QT-product, develop an algorithm for computing them, and present a large-scale test and a scalability analysis. In addition, we evaluate several rotation strategies based on the QT-polar decomposition through video rotation applications. The results show that the decomposition remains stable and maintains inter-frame consistency while accurately preserving colors.
item.dc:creator: Daochang Zhang, Yue Zhao, Jingqian Li, Dijana Mosic

item.title: An error control framework for computing the exponential of matrices arising from the finite element discretization
item.description: arXiv:2603.11871v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Several methods for computing the action of the matrix exponential $\mathrm{e}^{\boldsymbol{A}} \boldsymbol{b}$ are expressed by substituting $\boldsymbol{A}$ into a rational approximation of the scalar exponential function. When $\boldsymbol{A}$ is a general sparse matrix, the approximation error of such methods can be bounded using the numerical range of $\boldsymbol{A}$, which enables the computation of $\mathrm{e}^{\boldsymbol{A}} \boldsymbol{b}$ with a prescribed accuracy. This study extends this error control framework to matrices of the form $\boldsymbol{A} = \tau \boldsymbol{M}^{-1} \boldsymbol{K}$, where $\boldsymbol{M}$ is a well-conditioned symmetric positive definite matrix. A direct application of the framework faces two challenges: determining the numerical range of $\boldsymbol{A}$ is not straightforward, and the resulting error bounds can significantly overestimate the approximation error. In this paper, we show that these issues can be resolved by using the numerical range of the similarity transformed version of $\boldsymbol{A}$. Numerical experiments confirm that the computations can be performed within the prescribed error tolerance.
item.dc:creator: Fuminori Tatsuoka, Yuto Miyatake, Tomohiro Sogabe

item.title: Model Order Reduction for Parametric Hermitian Eigenvalue Problems: Local High-Order Approximation with Taylor-Reduced Basis Method
item.description: arXiv:2603.14620v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is concerned with the Taylor-reduced basis method (Taylor-RBM) for the efficient approximation of eigenspaces of large-scale parametric Hermitian matrices. The Taylor-RBM is a local model order reduction method, which constructs an approximation space by using the ranges of scaled derivatives of the spectral projector at a reference point in the parameter domain. For a prescribed order $n$, under local $\mathrm{C}^{n+1}$-regularity, we prove local convergence of orders $n+1$ and $2n+2$ for the eigenspace and the Ritz-value sum, respectively, and present a computationally efficient procedure for assembling the Taylor reduced basis space. Since this method is tightly connected to multivariate perturbation theory, we also analyze a projector approximation obtained from the finite Taylor polynomial of the eigenprojector and compare it with the Taylor-RBM.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Stamm, Zhuoyao Zeng

item.title: Stabilizing the Rayleigh--Ritz procedure by randomization
item.description: arXiv:2604.01037v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Extracting approximate eigenpairs from a prescribed subspace is of fundamental importance in eigenvalue computation. Although the standard Rayleigh--Ritz procedure is widely used for this purpose, it may suffer from deteriorated convergence of Ritz values and may even fail to produce convergent Ritz vectors, unless the compressed eigenvalue problem is assumed to be well-conditioned. In this paper, we address the eigenpair extraction problem by introducing a randomized Rayleigh--Ritz procedure. Our analysis shows that, for a simple eigenpair, the eigenvalue and eigenvector condition numbers of the randomly compressed generalized eigenvalue problem are, with high probability, comparable to those of the original problem, which yields a reliable approximate eigenpair from the extraction. The result also extends naturally to nonlinear eigenvalue problems.
item.dc:creator: Nian Shao

item.title: High-order kernel regularization of singular and hypersingular Helmholtz boundary integral operators
item.description: arXiv:2604.14797v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper extends and analyzes the high-order kernel regularization framework of Beale & Tlupova (arXiv:2510.13639) to all four on-surface boundary integral operators of the Helmholtz Calderon calculus in three dimensions: the single-layer, double-layer, adjoint double-layer, and hypersingular operators. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first high-order kernel regularization of the hypersingular operator for both the Helmholtz and Laplace equations in three dimensions. The regularization replaces each singular kernel with a smooth modification constructed from error functions together with a polynomial correction whose coefficients are determined through moment conditions. Alongside the derivation of the regularizing functions, the paper provides a unified error analysis of the combined regularization and quadrature discretization procedure. By coupling the regularization parameter to the mesh size, the two error contributions can be balanced, leading to explicit overall convergence rates that depend jointly on the order of the regularization and the degree of exactness of the surface quadrature rule. A key practical feature of the method is its implementation simplicity. Once the regularizing functions are determined, the numerical task reduces entirely to the evaluation of smooth surface integrals using standard quadrature, without the need for element-local solves, singularity-specific precomputations, or specialized quadrature rules. Although the modified kernel is generally incompatible with kernel-specific fast methods, this limitation is addressed through H-matrix acceleration, applicable in a black-box manner. Numerical examples -- including verification of the predicted convergence rates and solution of sound-soft and sound-hard scattering problems by smooth obstacles -- demonstrate the accuracy and practicality of the proposed methodology.
item.dc:creator: Luiz M. Faria, Carlos Perez-Arancibia, Svetlana Tlupova

item.title: Analytical and numerical study of nonlinear Riesz-Caputo boundary value problems
item.description: arXiv:2605.16102v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fractional boundary value problems are often used to model complex systems and processes characterized by memory effects and anomalous diffusion. In this paper, we consider nonlinear fractional boundary value problems of arbitrary order {\alpha} involving the Riesz-Caputo operator, which is particularly suited for modelling physical phenomena exhibiting symmetric diffusive effects. By reducing the problem to a dominant singular integral equation of Cauchy type and inverting it in closed form, we derive an integral representation of the solution, which we use to prove existence and uniqueness. The closed-form inversion also describes the typical behaviour of the solution near the endpoints of the interval and provides an exact singular solution, which we use as a test case. We then analyse a B-spline collocation method for the approximation of the solution, proving its convergence and illustrating it by numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: Enza Pellegrino, Francesca Pitolli, Chiara Sorgentone

item.title: High-Order Invariant-Domain Preserving Continuous Finite Elements via Graph-Poisson Convex Limiting
item.description: arXiv:2606.23397v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a high-order, locally conservative, invariant-domain preserving continuous finite element method for nonlinear scalar conservation laws. A first-order graph-viscosity scheme is built on the fine-$\mathbb P_1$ submesh induced by the high-order nodes, so that it remains compact and has positive lumped masses for every polynomial degree, while the high-order candidate can be any stabilized Galerkin method; here we use residual-based artificial viscosity and continuous interior penalty methods. The two updates conserve different discrete masses, and comparing each in its own conserved measure gives a nodal difference with zero sum, which a graph-Poisson problem represents as antisymmetric edge fluxes. For polynomial degrees with positive $\mathbb P_k$ lumped masses (e.g., $\mathbb P_1$, $\mathbb P_3$, $\mathbb P_5$ on triangles), convex limiting of these fluxes conserves the $\mathbb P_k$ mass exactly and in local flux form. For degrees with zero or negative lumped masses (e.g., $\mathbb P_2$, $\mathbb P_4$), limiting perturbs the mass only on the elements where it acts, and this perturbation is removed inside each such element without violating the bounds, exactly whenever the element has enough room within its bounds. Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order accuracy for smooth solutions, robustness near discontinuities, and agreement with the entropy solution on standard benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Murtazo Nazarov

item.title: Neural-Spectral and Newton-HUM Methods for Reconstructing Controls of Wave Equations
item.description: arXiv:2606.28029v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a framework for constructing and rigorously validating controls for semilinear wave equations with localized interior control. We analyze the continuous energy-space problem and certify exact control for finite-dimensional Galerkin systems. Under explicit smallness and neighborhood conditions, our a posteriori theorem proves the existence of an exact Galerkin control near a computed candidate. It combines a validated terminal-state error, a bounded right inverse of the derivative of the control-to-terminal-state map, and a Lipschitz bound for that derivative. Under additional uniform right-inverse and neighborhood conditions, we also show that Newton correction converges with quadratic decay of terminal-state errors. We use residual estimates and interval arithmetic to enclose the nonlinear trajectory and its linearized controllability Gramian. For the specified eight-mode tanh problem, we rigorously bound a source-response operator to prove contraction of the exact source-frozen iteration. We compare deterministic controls based on the Hilbert Uniqueness Method with neural approximations of temporal modal coefficients. Two Newton corrections reduce the computed terminal-state errors of all six tested neural candidates below $10^{-8}$. For the three certified candidates, we obtain smaller bounds on the distance to an exact Galerkin steering control by refining the validation mesh while keeping the computed controls fixed.
item.dc:creator: Tan-Phuc Nguyen, Minh-Binh Tran, Son Tu

item.title: Neural-Manifold Primal-Dual Model Order Reduction and Hyper-Reduction for Nonlinear Parametric Variational Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2607.21242v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a model order reduction framework for nonlinear parametrized variational inequalities arising in computational mechanics. The high-dimensional model is written in mixed primal-dual form with projection-based complementarity conditions, leading to nonlinear nonsmooth algebraic systems solved by a semi-smooth Newton method. On this basis, reduced models are constructed by proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) of both primal and dual solution snapshots. To address cases where low-dimensional linear spaces provide limited approximation efficiency, we introduce a neural-network-augmented reduced model. Two feedforward networks learn corrections in the truncated POD coordinates of the primal and dual variables from solutions of enlarged Galerkin ROMs. The learned reconstructions enter the coupled equilibrium and constraint equations directly, defining a nonlinear reduced system solved by approximate semi-smooth Newton iterations. The online cost associated with high-dimensional residual evaluations is reduced through hyper-reduction, using a sparse cubature approach based on greedy nonnegative least squares. The proposed methodology is assessed on two nonlinear variational inequalities with distinct sources of nonlinearity: a two-dimensional obstacle problem with a cubic nonlinearity in the state equation, and a three-dimensional frictional contact problem in which the Coulomb law induces a nonlinear projection in the constraint equation. Numerical results compare the high-dimensional model, the linear reduced model, the neural-network-augmented reduced model, and their hyper-reduced variants, demonstrating accurate approximations with substantial reductions in online computational cost. The performance study also evaluates feasibility over the complete constraint set and measures how errors in the reconstructed obstacle and contact forces affect the primal response.
item.dc:creator: Sofiane Ezzehi, Virginie Ehrlacher, Guillaume Ench\'ery, Thibault Faney

item.title: High-order $L^2$-Galerkin schemes for the decoupled potential integral equations
item.description: arXiv:2608.10799v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove Sobolev space well-posedness of the decoupled potential integral equations. Using basic pseudo-differential techniques, discrete stability is obtained for the standard $L^2$-pairing, and we deduce spectral convergence for high-order schemes employing discontinuous basis functions, or with additional element-wise tangential continuity imposed in the vectorial part of the system. The schemes are shown to be much better conditioned than a mature commercial EFIE/CFIE solver. In many cases appearing almost independent of wavenumber, mesh density, and the order.
item.dc:creator: David Scott Winterrose

item.title: Tensor-Train Isogeometric Analysis for Large-Scale Three-Dimensional Linear Elasticity
item.description: arXiv:2608.23595v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work develops tensor-train (TT) formulations for solving large-scale three-dimensional linear elasticity problems discretized by isogeometric analysis. By exploiting the tensor-product structure of the basis functions and the low-rank structure of geometry-dependent coefficient fields, the stiffness operator, mass operator, force vector, and displacement solution are represented in TT format. Two solution strategies are investigated: a block-operator formulation, in which the coupled elasticity operator is stored as separated TT blocks, and a single-operator formulation, in which the full coupled system is stored as one monolithic TT operator. A matrix-free three-field TT conjugate-gradient solver is introduced for the block formulation, while AMEn is used for the single-operator formulation. Numerical examples demonstrate substantial compression of both operators and solutions compared with conventional sparse full-grid representations, showing that TT-based formulations provide an efficient and scalable approach for large-scale three-dimensional elasticity simulations.
item.dc:creator: Quoc Thai Tran, Duc P. Truong, William Dai, Kim {\O}. Rasmussen

item.title: Hankel-Koopman Finite-Horizon Energy Decomposition of Coupled Experimental Data: A Three-Phase Data-Driven Twin Forecasting Framework
item.description: arXiv:2609.14501v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Finite-horizon prediction is challenging when observations are limited and a quantity of interest depends on several coupled nonlinear measurement channels. This paper develops a three-phase data-driven twin framework that integrates finite-horizon Hankel--Koopman energy decomposition, inverse-calibrated reconstruction using nonlinear autoregressive models with exogenous inputs, and forecast composition. Channel dynamics are identified and simulated in Hankel coefficient space, with candidate models assessed after reconstruction in physical measurement space. The resulting reduced-order model of the channel dynamics drives recursive prediction of the quantity of interest. Three theorems support the framework, establishing the energy decomposition and modal orthogonality; existence, uniqueness, and inverse stability of the auxiliary continuous inverse-calibration solution; and finite-horizon stability of the composed forecast for a fixed selected model under stated assumptions. A retrospective solar-power case study yields high correlations between predicted and reference trajectories across the considered forecast horizons, demonstrating reproduction of a constructed channels-dependent quantity of interest.
item.dc:creator: Diana A. Bistrian, Marcel Topor

item.title: Matrix nearness problems: Do real inputs admit real solutions?
item.description: arXiv:2609.14828v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a real square matrix $A$ and a nonempty closed target set of complex matrices $\mathcal{E}$, invariant by complex conjugation and containing real matrices, does the subset of $\mathcal{E}$ consisting of the matrices nearest to $A$ in the Frobenius distance always contain a real matrix? We give negative answers when $\mathcal{E}$ is either the set of normal matrices (solving a question posed by N. Higham) or the set of matrices whose eigenvalues lie in the closed left half-plane (solving a question posed by the first author and F. Poloni). For the latter problem, we also argue that the ratio between the real and complex distances is unbounded in every dimension $n\geq 3$, and this holds for every distance induced by a unitarily invariant norm. For both problems and $n \geq 3$, we show that a real input $A$ uniformly drawn from the unit sphere $\|A\|_F=1$ has no real minimizer over $\mathcal{E}$ with probability strictly between $0$ and $1$. Beyond these two cases, we prove for an arbitrary nonempty closed target sets $\mathcal{E}$ that, for almost every real input, either $\mathcal{E}$ contains a unique nearest matrix which is real, or every nearest matrix in $\mathcal{E}$ is nonreal.
item.dc:creator: Vanni Noferini, Matvei Zhukov

item.title: Element-wise Convergence Behavior of Subspace Iteration
item.description: arXiv:2609.21540v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies the element-wise convergence behavior of subspace iteration. All results are established for both \(\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{R}\) and \(\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{C}\). For a diagonal matrix \(\Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)\) with \(|\lambda_1|>\cdots>|\lambda_n|>0\), we analyze the modulus of each entry of the iterative matrix sequence generated by subspace iteration, both without and with the Rayleigh--Ritz procedure. Under mild assumptions on the initial matrix \(X\in\mathbb{F}^{n\times m}\), we first derive exact asymptotic expressions for \(|Q_k(i,j)|\) in the subspace iteration without the Rayleigh--Ritz procedure: entries with \(i\neq j\) decay as \(|\lambda_{\max\{i,j\}}/\lambda_{\min\{i,j\}}|^k\), and the deviation of \(|Q_k(j,j)|\) from \(1\) decays as \(\max\{|\lambda_j/\lambda_{j-1}|,|\lambda_{j+1}/\lambda_j|\}^{2k}\), with explicit coefficients determined by the LU factorization of \(X\). Similar conclusions could also be established for upper triangular matrices. For the Rayleigh--Ritz variant, we obtain element-wise bounds for the normalized Ritz vectors \(Z_k\). Specifically, for \(|Z_k(i,j)|\), off-diagonal entries with \(i\geq m+1\) decay as \((|\lambda_i|/|\lambda_j|)^k\), off-diagonal entries with \(i\leq m\) decay as \((|\lambda_{m+1}|^2/(|\lambda_i||\lambda_j|))^k\), and the deviation of \(|Z_k(j,j)|\) from \(1\) decays as \((|\lambda_{m+1}|/|\lambda_j|)^{2k}\). These results give an element-wise description of the convergence behavior of subspace iteration. After an orthogonal or unitary change of basis, the results could be further generalized.
item.dc:creator: Mingyang Zhao

item.title: Toeplitz Infinite GMRES for Parameterized Linear Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.01740v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop Toeplitz infinite GMRES for solving large sparse analytic parameterized systems $A(s)x(s)=z$ at many parameter values. Our method exploits a block upper triangular Toeplitz structure in the companion Krylov sequence to construct the Arnoldi process and recover solution approximations without storing full Arnoldi vectors. We derive incremental recurrences requiring $\mathcal{O}(np^2+p^3)$ arithmetic and $\mathcal{O}(np+p^2)$ storage for $p$ Arnoldi steps, excluding factorization setup and assuming linear-cost coefficient actions and triangular solves. A dynamic generator-refreshing strategy addresses cancellation in this basic recurrence. Moreover, we show that the Arnoldi basis can be simply represented using one block row and a nilpotent matrix. For $A(s)$ admitting a split form, we further use this structure to develop an implicitly rebased method. A residual lower bound for square-summable Taylor coefficients explains the effect of scaling outside the unit disk. Theoretical analysis and numerical experiments illustrate the computational efficiency of the proposed methods.
item.dc:creator: Weiguo Gao, Feiyang Jiang

item.title: Error Estimates in Physics-Informed Neural Networks to Heat-Wave Fluid-Structure Interactive System
item.description: arXiv:2610.03575v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a physics-informed neural network (PINN) approximation of a coupled PDE system that models the interaction between fluid and elastic dynamics. The canonical heat-wave model considered here couples a parabolic and a hyperbolic equation through transmission conditions on a fixed boundary interface, and serves as a prototype for the Stokes-elastic systems that arises in real world applications. This coupling makes the error analysis more delicate than that for a single PDE. We bound the error between the exact and PINN solutions by the associated PINN residuals, and we moreover prove that the generalization error is controlled by the training error, the number of quadrature points, and the size of the network. {To the best of our knowledge}, these are the first error estimates for a PINN approximation of a coupled fluid-structure interaction PDE system. We also show that numerical experiments with respect to a given test problem.
item.dc:creator: Pelin G. Geredeli, Mohammad Mahabubur Rahman, Deepanshu Verma

item.title: Improved algorithms for computing the matrix logarithm based on the double-exponential formula
item.description: arXiv:2610.25361v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Tatsuoka et al. proposed an efficient algorithm for computing the matrix logarithm using the double-exponential (DE) formula. Its discretization error decreases exponentially as the number of quadrature nodes grows, and its nested grids allow previously computed values to be reused when the mesh is refined. They also reported that their approach is more robust than Gauss--Legendre quadrature for ill-conditioned matrices. We propose two algorithms based on the DE formula. The first adaptively refines the mesh while reusing previously computed values and requires no matrix norm computations. The second uses a rigorous error bound to select the number of quadrature nodes a priori. Numerical experiments show that both methods attain lower errors than Tatsuoka et al.'s method at comparable elapsed times over the tested ranges.
item.dc:creator: Tomoaki Okayama, Tsubasa Setogawa

item.title: A fast Laguerre--Fourier spectral method for the polyatomic Boltzmann collision operator with continuous internal energy
item.description: arXiv:2610.25921v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The polyatomic Boltzmann equation extends the classical kinetic description to gases whose molecules possess internal energy in addition to their translational motion. The distribution function then has one more variable than in the monatomic case, and the collision operator becomes an eight-fold integral whose evaluation dominates the cost of solving the equation. In this work, we propose a fast Laguerre--Fourier spectral method for the polyatomic Boltzmann equation with continuous internal energy, which evaluates the collision operator in $O(K^2MN^4\log N + K^3MN^4)$ online operations after a solution-independent precomputation, where $N$ is the number of Fourier modes in each velocity direction, $K$ is the number of Laguerre modes and $M$ is the number of quadrature points on the sphere. Specifically, the distribution function is expanded in generalized Laguerre functions in the internal energy and in Fourier modes in velocity. A sequence of changes of variables then separates the internal-energy integrals from the velocity convolutions, so that the former no longer involve the distribution function and are computed once and stored. Numerical experiments are presented for both the spatially homogeneous and the spatially inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation. They confirm the spectral accuracy of the proposed method and its agreement with the direct simulation Monte Carlo method.
item.dc:creator: Pei Zhang, Yanli Wang, Zhenning Cai

item.title: Structure-Preserving Numerical Schemes for a Time-Fractional Porous Medium Equation with Nonlocal Pressure
item.dc:creator: {\L}ukasz P{\l}ociniczak, Hubert Woszczek

item.title: Deflation-Based Spectral Preconditioning for the Conjugate Gradient Method on Perturbed Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.28808v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider sequences of large symmetric positive-definite linear systems in which spectral information from a reference matrix $A$ is reused to accelerate the solution of a nearby system with perturbed matrix $A(t)=A+tE$, where $E$ is symmetric, $\|E\|_F=1$, and $t\geq0$ is the perturbation size. We compare deflated conjugate gradient (deflated CG) with preconditioned CG (PCG) equipped with a scaled spectral preconditioner constructed from the same spectral information of $A$. First, we derive an energy-norm error characterization of deflated CG. We then use perturbation analysis to show that, after one additional PCG iteration, the squared PCG error is bounded, up to terms of order $t^2$, by an explicit multiple of the squared deflated CG error. This result clarifies the role of the scaling parameter in the preconditioner. Experiments show that the scaled spectral preconditioner recovers much of the convergence improvement provided by deflation while requiring fewer products with $A(t)$.
item.dc:creator: Youssef Diouane, Selime G\"urol, Oussama Mouhtal, Dominique Orban

item.title: Globally Optimal Solutions to a Class of Fractional Optimization Problems Based on Proximal Gradient Algorithm
item.description: arXiv:2306.11286v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper investigates a category of constrained fractional optimization problems that emerge in various practical applications. The objective function for this category is characterized by the ratio of a numerator and denominator, both being convex, semi-algebraic and differentiable with Lipschitz continuous gradients over the constraint sets. The constrained sets associated with these problems are closed, convex, and semi-algebraic. We propose an efficient algorithm that is inspired by the proximal gradient method, and we provide a thorough convergence analysis. Our algorithm is shown to converge to a critical point without the typical need for a nonnegative numerator, and this critical point becomes a globally optimal solution whenever the numerator is nonpositive at the initial point. Our approach is adaptable to unbounded constraint sets as well. Therefore, our approach is viable for many more practical models. Numerical experiments show that our method not only reliably reaches ground-truth solutions in some model problems but also outperforms several existing methods in maximizing the Sharpe ratio with real-world financial data.
item.dc:creator: Yizun Lin, Jian-Feng Cai, Zhao-Rong Lai, Cheng Li

item.title: Compressing multivariate functions with tree tensor networks
item.description: arXiv:2410.03572v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Tensor networks are a compressed format for multi-dimensional data. One dimensional tensor networks -- often referred to as tensor trains (TT) or matrix product states (MPS) -- are increasingly being used as a numerical ansatz for continuum functions by ``quantizing'' the inputs into discrete binary digits. Here we demonstrate the power of more general tree tensor networks (TTNs) for this purpose. We provide direct constructions of a number of elementary functions as generic tree tensor networks and interpolative constructions for more complicated functions via a generalization of the tensor cross interpolation algorithm. For a range of multi-dimensional functions we show how more structured tree tensor networks offer a significantly more efficient ansatz than the commonly used tensor train. Finally, we demonstrate how the methods introduced in this work can be used to realize a TTN-based solver for multi-dimensional, non-linear Fredholm equations.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Tindall, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Ryan Levy

item.title: Diagonally-Weighted Generalized Method of Moments Estimation for Gaussian Mixture Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2507.20459v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With direct computation of moments through order $L$ in $d$ dimensions, standard method of moments (MM) incurs $\Omega(d^L)$ computation and storage costs, and standard generalized method of moments (GMM) additionally requires estimating and inverting an often ill-conditioned covariance matrix of size $\Omega(d^L)$-by-$\Omega(d^L)$ to obtain the optimal weighting matrix. Pereira, Kileel, and Kolda [arXiv:2202.06930 (2022)] avoid the tensor computation cost of MM through implicit moment computation. Despite this progress, incorporating statistically principled weighting while preserving computational efficiency remains an important challenge, particularly at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), where sampling variances can differ substantially across moment orders. We introduce diagonally-weighted GMM (DGMM), which assigns one adaptive weight to each moment order through a structured approximation of the optimal weighting matrix while avoiding the covariance inversion, thereby balancing statistical efficiency, computational complexity, and numerical stability. For general parametric models, we prove that DGMM is consistent, asymptotically normal, and near-efficient under explicit structural conditions. For heteroscedastic low-rank Gaussian mixtures, we design a computationally efficient and numerically stable algorithm that extends the implicit moment computation to the DGMM objective, gradients, and weights and incorporates Nystr\"om approximations of the kernel sums. In low-SNR experiments with $d=100$ and $L=4$, where standard MM and GMM are infeasible, controlled weighting comparisons show that DGMM achieves consistently small parameter errors across tested initializations, including the challenging starts where alternative weightings struggle, with shorter median runtimes and fewer iterations. The code and data will be available upon publication at https://github.com/liu-lzhang/dgmm.
item.dc:creator: Liu Zhang, Oscar Mickelin, Sheng Xu, Amit Singer

item.title: Reservoir computing based predictive reduced order model for steel grade intermixing in an industrial continuous casting tundish
item.description: arXiv:2509.26293v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Continuous casting is a widely adopted process in the steel industry, where maintaining high steel quality is paramount. Efficient prediction of grade intermixing during ladle changeover operations is critical for maintaining steel quality and minimizing material losses in the continuous casting process. Among various factors influencing grade intermixing, operating parameters play a significant role, in addition to tundish geometry and flow control devices. In this study, three-dimensional, transient, two-phase turbulent flow simulations are conducted to investigate the ladle changeover operation. During this process, the molten steel level in the tundish typically varies over time, significantly affecting the grade intermixing phenomena. The influence of ladle change time on intermixing time has been presented. However, high-fidelity full-order simulations of such complex transient phenomena are computationally expensive and are impractical for real-time monitoring or design-space exploration in industrial-scale applications. To address this issue, a reduced order modelling approach based on proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) and reservoir computing (RC) is employed to efficiently predict intermixing time. The proposed reduced order model (ROM) demonstrates excellent predictive accuracy using limited training data while requiring significantly less computational resources and training time. The results demonstrate the potential of the proposed methodology as a fast, reliable tool for real-time process monitoring and optimization in industrial continuous casting operations.
item.dc:creator: Harshith Gowrachari, Mattia Giuseppe Barra, Giovanni Stabile, Gianluca Bazzaro, Gianluigi Rozza

item.title: When Does Cheap Physics Help? Gated Multi-Fidelity Physics-Informed Networks with Provable Sample Savings and Conformal Guarantees
item.description: arXiv:2602.01176v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: High-fidelity (HF) simulations of parametric partial differential equations are expensive, whereas low-fidelity (LF) models such as coarse grids or simplified physics are cheap but biased. Multi-fidelity physics-informed neural networks combine the two, yet it remains unclear when cheap physics actually reduces the number of HF solves, and existing methods silently fail when the LF model is misleading and offer no guaranteed uncertainty. We answer the first question with a sharp sample-complexity bound: learning the HF field through its discrepancy from the LF model reduces the number of HF samples needed for accuracy $\varepsilon$ by the factor $\kappa^{2\gamma}$, where $\kappa$ is the ratio of the complexity of the discrepancy to that of the HF field and $\gamma$ is the effective-dimension exponent, and we confirm the predicted scaling with exact risk computations in a kernel model. Guided by the analysis, we propose GaMF-PINN, a gated multi-fidelity PINN that learns where to trust the LF model and falls back to physics-only learning where it does not, together with a function-level conformal procedure that returns uncertainty bands containing the entire HF solution with probability at least $1-\alpha$ in finite samples. We release MFPDE-Bench, an open benchmark of paired LF/HF solvers for four parametric PDEs with coarse-grid and simplified-physics LF models. Across MFPDE-Bench, GaMF-PINN reaches the accuracy of a standard HF-PINN with up to 8x fewer HF solves, remains robust when the LF model is deliberately corrupted, and attains the nominal coverage where Bayesian PINNs and deep ensembles under-cover.
item.dc:creator: Olaf Yunus Laitinen Imanov, Rana Irem Turhan, Isgandar Jafarli

item.title: Formulation and Learning Of The Forecasting Problem
item.description: arXiv:2603.20359v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Machine learning has opened new frontiers in purely data-driven forecasting of dynamical systems; the resulting methods are showing considerable promise in some application domains. However, in contrast to model-driven algorithms, analysis of these data-driven methods is poorly developed. In this paper we address this issue, developing a theory to underpin data-driven methods to solve forecasting problems. The theoretical framework comprises two key components: (i) establishing the existence of a mapping defining the forecasting problem; (ii) showing that it is possible to approximate this mapping by supervised learning techniques, to arbitrary accuracy. We work in the continuous-time and noise-free setting as this defines a simple canonical setting in which to establish an underpinning theory; the continuous-time setting leads to an operator formulation of the problem in which the underlying forecasting map is defined on pathspace. As a byproduct of our framework we show that analogous existence and approximation results may be obtained for the smoothing problem of recovering unobserved components of dynamical systems, from observed components, using supervised learning. The theoretical results, for both forecasting and smoothing, are illustrated with experiments studying the Lorenz `63, Lorenz `96 and Kuramoto-Sivashinsky dynamical systems.
item.dc:creator: Edoardo Calvello, Elizabeth Carlson, Nikola Kovachki, Michael N. Manta, Andrew M. Stuart

item.title: Generalization of Zeroth-Order Method for Quotients of Quadratic Functions
item.description: arXiv:2604.26913v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Optimization of quadratic functions and their quotients is relevant in subspace and iterative optimization methods. In this paper, we consider the matrix-free computation of the generalized operator norm and the maximization of a generalized Rayleigh quotient when only forward evaluations of two linear operators $A$ and $B$ are available. The proposed method samples search directions uniformly from the full unit sphere, thereby avoiding tangent-space sampling and explicit access to the metric matrix $B^{\mathrm T}B$. The exact line search along each sampled direction reduces to a $2\times2$ generalized eigenvalue problem on specific Gram matrices. In the generic case its maximizing step has a closed form. We prove that the objective values converge almost surely to the largest generalized eigenvalue and that the distance of the iterates to the leading generalized eigenspace converges to zero. We also relate full-sphere moment estimators to the Riemannian gradient and Hessian. The numerical experiments on synthetic Gau{\ss}ian operators illustrate the behavior of the methods, and further studies of the proposed algorithms indicate favorable empirical convergence and weak dependence on the tested problem dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Bresch

item.title: Numerical study of the 2D Kaup-Broer-Kuperschmidt Boussinesq system
item.description: arXiv:2605.05183v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work we consider the well posed version of the Kaup-Broer-Kuperschmidt system in two dimensions. We numerically construct soliton type solutions and show that they are unstable both against dispersion and singularity formation. Further, we study line solitons and their stability, as well as generally localised initial data. In either case we fail to find stable structures.
item.dc:creator: Th\'eo Gaudry, Christian Klein, Jean-Claude Saut, Nikola Stoilov

item.title: Differentiable FEM versus PINN for pavement layer inverse analysis: enforcing physics as hard or soft constraints
item.description: arXiv:2606.03210v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Automatic-differentiation-based inverse analysis methods, including physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and differentiable programming, have recently shown great promise due to their ability to compute accurate gradients and convergence efficiency. However, their applicability to falling weight deflectometer (FWD) backcalculation remains unexplored. This study critically evaluates PINN-based inverse analysis for a multilayer pavement system and investigates differentiable finite element method (DiffFEM) as an alternative based on a synthetic benchmark. The standard PINN does not recover layer moduli because of the sharp domain discontinuities inherent to layered pavement systems. Although we use an extended PINN with domain decomposition (XPINN), which shows better performance on discontinuous domains, its performance remains highly sensitive to loss weighting and network architecture, and degrades under measurement noise. By contrast, DiffFEM consistently achieves more accurate, stable, and computationally efficient inversion results. These results show and quantify the expected advantage of DiffFEM, which enforces the governing physics as a hard constraint in the solver, over PINN-based approaches, where the governing physics is imposed as a soft constraint through the loss function. More broadly, the findings suggest that the choice between PINN- and DiffFEM-based inverse analysis needs careful consideration, with DiffFEM offering practical advantages when an efficient and robust differentiable forward solver is available.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Computer-Aided Civil and Infrastructure Engineering, Vol. 51, 100251 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Yongjin Choi, Hyeonbin Moon, Seunghwa Ryu

item.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for coupled stiff transport systems
item.description: arXiv:2606.21236v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) struggle with stiff, regime-changing transport equations due to instability, loss imbalance, and violations of physical consistency. This paper investigates these failures through the Marshak wave equations, a canonical benchmark from radiative transport, where initial and boundary conditions differ by up to 12 orders of magnitude, and proposes modifications to the standard PINN framework to overcome them. Three modifications are introduced: a ScaledSigmoid final activation enforcing physical bounds and positivity of the unknowns; a logarithmic MSE loss replacing the standard quadratic loss for initial and boundary conditions, enabling training across extreme scale disparities; and explicit enforcement of global conservation laws as an additional physics loss term. Monte Carlo sampling with exponential time weighting is used throughout. The proposed framework recovers the Marshak wave dynamics - including the hot, cold, and wave-front regions - in good agreement with a reference Implicit Monte Carlo solution (sub-millimeter absolute error on the front position, although the relative error remains substantial at early times), with run times under 5 minutes. Ablation studies confirm that each ingredient is essential: linear activation, absence of the logarithmic loss, or removal of the PDE term each independently cause the method to fail qualitatively. This work identifies and resolves three concrete failure modes of standard PINN on stiff hyperbolic systems with nonlinear coupling. The combination of bounded activations, scale-aware loss functions, and conservation law enforcement constitutes a framework validated on the present one-dimensional Marshak wave problem, with potential extension to other coupled stiff transport systems in engineering.
item.dc:creator: Laetitia Laguzet, Gabriel Turinici

item.title: Current-Sheet Formation in Electron Magnetohydrodynamics with Split Fractional Dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2607.18648v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Thin current sheets are central small-scale structures in electron magnetohydrodynamics (EMHD), closely associated with energy dissipation and fast magnetic reconnection at electron scales. We study their formation numerically in a $2\frac{1}{2}$-dimensional EMHD system on a periodic domain with split fractional dissipation, where the magnetic potential and the vertical magnetic component are damped separately. The local theory is governed by a symmetric combined damping balance, but the numerical onset of small-scale growth need not follow this symmetry. A scaling analysis identifies the out-of-plane current as the primary concentration observable, since it is regularized only through the magnetic-potential equation. Using a validated Fourier pseudospectral exponential time-differencing solver with resolution-controlled diagnostics, we find a clear decay/concentration dichotomy. The onset boundary is markedly asymmetric: current-sheet formation appears to be controlled mainly by damping of the magnetic potential, rather than by the combined damping strength. The analyticity strip collapses to the grid scale, the concentration sharpens under grid refinement, and the observed growth is consistent with an energy-critical self-similar rate, with exponent near three. These experiments indicate that magnetic-potential damping is the apparent binding constraint for current-sheet concentration, refining the symmetric sum picture.
item.dc:creator: Ruimeng Hu, Qirui Peng, Xu Yang

item.title: Mirror descent algorithms with logarithmic barriers
item.description: arXiv:2608.22834v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive convergence guarantees for mirror descent and proximal mirror descent with a logarithmic barrier as the distance-generating function. When the solution lies on the boundary, the Bregman divergence blows up and classical guarantees become vacuous. While existing remedies recover $O(\log k/k)$ rates by adapting classical bounds, we propose a more direct route in which the Bregman distance to the solution never appears, and which achieves the same rate with constant stepsize. We also construct an example showing that this rate cannot be improved in general. Finally, we compare the proposed approach with interior-point methods.
item.dc:creator: Alberto De Marchi, Yura Malitsky, Adrien B. Taylor

item.title: An Energy-Based Conservative-Dissipative Latent Neural Evolution Operator for Magnetization Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2609.04530v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a reduced-order learning framework that couples a convolutional autoencoder to a structured latent neural ordinary differential equation. A learned scalar generates the latent dynamics through an antisymmetric operator and a positive-definite dissipative operator. The antisymmetric component permits motion along scalar level sets, while the dissipative component decreases the scalar. Adding a coercive quadratic term gives bounded continuous-time latent trajectories and approach to the scalar's critical set under the stated assumptions. The scalar provides a structural constraint rather than an approximation of physical energy. The encoder, decoder, scalar, and operators are trained jointly on short snapshot windows without time-derivative supervision, physical-energy labels, or dissipation penalties. At inference, one initial state is encoded and evolved continuously in latent space, with decoding only at requested times. We demonstrate the framework on micromagnetic magnetization trajectories from NIST $\mu$MAG Standard Problem 4 and compare it with dissipative-only dynamics and an unstructured latent neural differential equation. Repeated training runs show competitive observed-horizon accuracy, while selected longer rollouts illustrate improved retention of approximately stationary states relative to the unstructured baseline. These results motivate scalar-generated latent dynamics as an inductive bias for reduced-order prediction and other learning tasks where bounded evolution and equilibrium behavior are important.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Schaffer, Lukas Exl
